Lin S.role: Co-author of the 2008 mouse study showing that muscle needs raptor, the mTORC1 component, to stay healthy
story: Shuo Lin is the fourth of thirteen authors on a 2008 study in Cell Metabolism from the Biozentrum in Basel. The team removed raptor, a key part of the growth-control complex mTORC1, only in the skeletal muscle of mice. These muscles slowly became dystrophic and the mice did not live long. Removing rictor, the matching part of mTORC2, had no such effect. The work was done in mice, so it shows what mTORC1 does in mouse muscle, not directly in people.

PubMed does not list an affiliation for Shuo Lin in this 2008 record. The Biozentrum, University of Basel link comes from a 2013 muscle paper on mTORC1 in atrophy and hypertrophy, where Shuo Lin appears next to the same group members (Bentzinger, Romanino, Hall and Rüegg), and a 2019 raptor paper from the same institute. The Atlas does not carry a source for the person's role, training or current position.

highlights.BEN2008: Fourth of thirteen authors on the paper that deleted raptor or rictor in mouse skeletal muscle.
